a never-before-seen event is processed

a retry after a FAILED attempt is allowed through, not skipped

only one state in the whole space reports duplicate
every state in the space yields a well-formed disposition

an empty token cannot match an empty secret

a secret exactly at the minimum length is accepted
not-configured is reported as 503, never 401
the correct token is authorised

a token that is a prefix of the secret is rejected
a token with the secret as a prefix is rejected
a missing header is missing-token, distinct from bad-token
matching is case sensitive on the token itself
the scheme is case insensitive, the token is not touched

a non-bearer scheme yields nothing
a bearer scheme with no token yields nothing
non-string input yields nothing rather than throwing
equal strings compare equal
different strings compare unequal
different lengths compare unequal, including prefixes

null and undefined are treated as empty, not as wildcards
multibyte characters compare correctly
every position is compared, not just the first mismatch

suites.title: a check that could not run must not read as an all-clear

specs.title: unconfigured says so and explicitly denies being an all-clear
a failed query says so and denies being an all-clear
a genuinely clean result is the ONLY output that reassures
clean output names the window it checked, so a short window cannot hide behind it
a single session converts minor units to a readable amount
amounts are summed across sessions, not counted
a null amount does not poison the total with NaN
currency comes from the data, not hardcoded, and survives a null first row

suites.title: each row says what actually went wrong

specs.title: never_claimed is called out as a probably-missing webhook
a claimed-but-failed row reports its status and error
a missing email is stated rather than rendered as undefined
every row appears, not just the first
the report never renders the literal word undefined for any row shape

suites.title: reading the timestamp out of the header

specs.title: pulls t out of a real stripe-signature header
tolerates surrounding whitespace, a leading +, and extra schemes
does not mistake another key ending in t for the timestamp
reports a present-but-unreadable t as PRESENT, which is what fails it shut
refuses an integer too large to be exact, and still reports it present
reports absent for anything that is not a string
the reproduction case: 600s ahead is rejected
exactly on the tolerance boundary is accepted, one second past it is not
a wildly future timestamp, the unbounded-validity case, is rejected
a present-but-unparseable t is REFUSED, not waved through
malformed and absent are different verdicts, which is the whole fix
a malformed t is refused no matter what the clock says

suites.title: everything else is allowed, on purpose

specs.title: the past is left entirely to Stripe tolerance
an ABSENT t degrades OPEN and says so
a broken clock degrades OPEN under its OWN reason code
a valid in-window timestamp is a clean pass, not a degrade

suites.title: mutation guard: the split is exact, so neither always-answer survives

specs.title: a sweep of offsets rejects precisely the ones past tolerance
the sweep is sensitive to the comparison, so it cannot pass vacuously
